decisions.statement: The command tree and the folder tree under `command/` are one tree said twice.
A command and a namespace are judged here rather than every page under a domain.
The page above one judged is the page naming it among its parts.
A page under `command/` is input here though that page is no level of the tree.
A change to a page's parts leaves every page that page names judged.
A page the `command` page type names sits in a folder directly in `command/pages/`.
Any other page judged sits in a folder directly inside its parent's own folder.
A folder is named for what its page's slug adds to the parent's slug.
A page whose slug opens with anything but its parent's slug is refused for that.
A command's slug is its path under `command/pages` with a hyphen for each slash.
A level's own name is the folder that level sits in.
A level of the command tree names itself with no name of a level above it.
A command or a namespace is named among the parts of a namespace or of the `command` page type.
Whether a namespace names an area worth narrowing by is judged by its writer rather than here.
A module under `command/pages` sits under the lowest level every page reaching it sits under.
A page reaching a module counts at the lowest level that page sits under.
A page the change adds counts among the pages reaching a module.
A level the change adds is a level of the tree.
The levels and the modules of the tree are read from the index the change leaves.
The files of a module's own folder are what git carries there as the change leaves it.
A module reached from two levels with no level above both sits in `command/modules`.
A module no page under `command/pages` reaches sits in `command/modules` as well.
A page outside `command/pages` reaching a module is counted by nothing here.
A change to a body under `command/` leaves every module under `command/pages` judged.
No page type is named here beyond the command, the namespace and the module.
A module under `command/` is named among the parts of a page under `command/`.
A module under `command/pages` is named among the parts of the command or the namespace beside it.
A module under `command/pages` sits in a folder directly inside the folder of the page naming it.
A module's own name is judged by nothing here.
A body mentioning or implementing the tree is judged by a syntax rule rather than here.

definition: the check refusing a command, a namespace or a module misplaced or misnamed in the command tree
